newsitem.title: INDIA: Bharat Petroleum to build $70 mln terminal.
newsitem.headline: Bharat Petroleum to build $70 mln terminal.

text.p: India's state-run refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd will build a 2.5 billion rupee ($69.83 million) liquefied petroleum gas import terminal in eastern India, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Friday.
The news agency said the company planned to invest 8.32 billion rupees in eastern India over the next five years.

PTI quoted company director V.K. Raina as saying the new terminal, to be set up at Paradeep port in the state of Orissa, would have a capacity of six million tonnes per annum. The LPG for the terminal would be imported from the Middle East.
Raina said the firm planned to invest a total of 3.96 billion rupees in Orissa, nearly 2.36 billion rupees in the neighbouring state of West Bengal and another two billion rupees in Bihar.

PTI quoted Raina as saying the LPG supply gap in the eastern Indian states, currently more than 300,000 tonnes, could widen to 600,000 tonnes by 2002. He said the Paradeep terminal was expected to bridge the gap.
India produces 3.2 million tonnes of LPG and imports 7.0 million tonnes.
LPG availability is expected to improve in 1997/98 (April-March) when imports will reach 2.5 million tonnes, and domestic production 3.5 million tonnes, PTI said.
The Indian government holds 66.2 percent of Bharat Petroleum's equity. The public, Indian financial institutions and foreign investors hold the rest.
